newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed down on Thursday on weak market sentiment fanned by renewed rumours that the securities authorities would bar domestic investors from buying new B shares, brokers said.
The index fell 0.133 points or 0.26 percent to 50.455 points, on volume of 5.9 million shares worth $2.4 million. Of 41 B shares, 35 traded, with 15 down, eight flat and 12 up.

Brokers said there were rumours that the top securities watchdog, China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), would impose a ban on domestic investors. Such rumours have circulated many times in the market. A CSRC spokeswoman declined comment.
The B market is theoretically open only to overseas investors but brokers say about 50 percent of trading in Shanghai is conducted by locals.
Brokers said few investors wanted to build positions because of poor sentiment and that light selling late in the session sent the index down, wiping out morning gains.
"Investors had no interest in buying because of talk of renewed restrictions on domestic investors," one broker said. "It is difficult for the market to rise before the rumour is clarified."
"The index is likely to test the key 50-point support level on Friday," said a second broker. "But some major domestic institutions are expected to support the market."
Shanghai Automation Instrumentation was the day's worst performer on disappointing interim results, falling $0.014 or 8.04 percent to $0.160, on volume of 150,000 shares.

Shanghai Erfangji Textile Machinery bucked the trend on a technical rebound with its price having fallen sharply in recent days, traders said. The stock rose $0.004 or 3.99 percent to $0.104, on volume of 123,700 shares.
Heilongjiang Electric Power traded the most, gaining $0.004 or 1.11 percent to $0.364, on volume of 680,900 shares.

Shanghai's A share index closed down, reversing morning gains, despite positive news that the city government would support listed firms by cutting their income tax rate to 15 percent from 33 percent. Brokers said the market was under heavy pressure with a rapid pace of new share issues and listings.

It lost 13.016 points or 1.62 percent to 790.814 points, on volume of 244.415 million shares worth 2.1 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index slipped 47.338 points or 2.29 percent to 2019.021. - Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
